# HEM v0.7.4b5 — Home Assistant lifecycle fixes

- Stops HEM scheduling as soon as Home Assistant begins stopping, including a full restart or shutdown that does not unload integration entries. Cancels controller timers, pending notices and optional background work before draining cleanup.
- Gives HEM cleanup a shared 10-second budget followed by a brief cancellation drain. If cleanup fails or cannot finish, an integration reload refuses to start a replacement manager over unfinished work. A full Home Assistant stop does not begin the legacy reload-only safe-OFF command sequence.
- Restores saved state with up to four independent loads at once and sanitizes environment history in the executor. Presence history still loads before arrival preparation, and all required restoration finishes before control starts. Interrupted startup cannot overwrite unread environment history with an empty snapshot.
- Defers saved PID reviews and automatic announcements until Home Assistant is running. Optional delivery uses owned background tasks, and direct notification/TTS calls have a 10-second deadline. Existing Announcement Hub acknowledgment behavior is preserved.
- Coalesces entity, device and area registry bursts before rebuilding the fault index. The existing startup dashboard debounce remains in place.
- Preserves PID gains, committed review receipts, physical-device ownership, minimum operating times and restart journals. Adds tests for full Home Assistant lifecycle events, interrupted restoration, late callbacks, notification cancellation and incomplete cleanup.

The cleanup budget covers HEM's awaited teardown. Home Assistant's own final storage writes, other integrations and operating-system shutdown can still take additional time. This release does not force physical devices off during a full Home Assistant stop.

Update through HACS with beta versions enabled, restart Home Assistant to load the integration, and reload the dashboard.
